picks.rationale: Neural acoustic modelling replaces multi-gigabyte orchestral sample libraries — the biggest change to a composer's disk and articulation workflow this week; MusicRadar chosen as the single source for this triple-covered launch (KVR/SOS dropped).
picks.excerpt: Dreamtonics' Instrument X promises a full range of expressive classical instruments with a tiny disk footprint, replacing multi-gigabyte orchestral sample libraries with neural modelling. MusicRadar frames it as a potential end to the 'bigger library = better sound' era for composers and scorers.

picks.rationale: sonible folds its whole AI-assisted plugin line into one intelligent channel strip, turning scattered smart: tools into a single mixing chain a producer can drop on every track tomorrow.
picks.excerpt: sonible's smart:chain bundles the company's AI-assisted processors into a single intelligent channel strip covering EQ, compression, de-harshing, gating, input riding and saturation. It positions sonible's 'smart' analysis as a whole mixing ecosystem rather than a set of separate plugins.

picks.rationale: Abyss II turns any dropped audio file into ML-grouped spectral 'Tone Colors', a concrete new way to mine an existing sample folder instead of generating from a prompt.
picks.excerpt: Dawesome's Abyss II turns any dropped audio file into a sequence of playable spectral 'Tone Colors', using machine learning to extract and group similar results into a custom palette. It reframes sample libraries as raw material for a visual, gesture-driven synth.

picks.rationale: Section-level regeneration and per-section lyric rewrites move generative music from one-shot rolls to actual arrangement editing — the first real editing surface in a prompt-to-song tool.
picks.excerpt: ElevenLabs has added 'Composer' to ElevenMusic, letting users edit and regenerate individual sections of a generated track without changing the rest. Users can rewrite lyrics per section, compare multiple takes and rearrange song structure by swapping, doubling or extending sections.

picks.rationale: TikTok's SoundOn signing an openly AI-assisted creator is the first test of how a major platform packages and monetises that workflow — the commercial counterpart to this week's tool news.
picks.excerpt: TikTok's distribution arm SoundOn has signed Gina Jones, the creator behind AI-assisted viral project 'Gina's Pet Bangers'. It is one of the first major-platform signings of an openly AI-assisted creator, and a test of how labels package that workflow.
